title: Romance on every boulevard
clues: A storied city shaped by a winding river that splits it into left and right banks.
Known for grand 19th‑century avenues and a star of roads radiating from a famous arch.
An uprising here in 1789 began with the storming of a prison and shook a monarchy.
Impressionist pioneer Claude Monet was born here before honing his craft along its quays.
Home to an iron lattice tower and a museum crowned by a glass pyramid.

title: Baroque charm in the shadow of the Alps
clues: A picturesque city framed by snow-capped peaks with a river cutting through its historic core.
Its old town is famed for ornate Baroque facades and is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A commanding hilltop fortress has guarded the skyline since the 11th century.
A beloved 1965 musical about a singing governess immortalized its hills and gardens on film.
It’s the birthplace of a prodigious composer, whose childhood home on Getreidegasse is now a museum.

title: Where Modernism Meets the Mediterranean
clues: A sun-kissed Mediterranean metropolis celebrated for beaches, tapas, and lively plazas.
Its waterfront was dramatically reshaped for a Summer Olympics that propelled it onto the global stage in the early 1990s.
A cradle of avant‑garde art that fostered Joan Miró, who’s honored with a hilltop museum.
A tree-lined promenade buzzing with buskers leads to a beloved market famed for jamón and fresh juices.
Fantastical spires of an unfinished basilica by Antoni Gaudí dominate the skyline.

title: Where East Meets West
clues: A vast metropolis that bridges two continents, split by a storied strait crisscrossed by ferries.
For centuries, it was the seat of Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman power.
An iconic domed monument here has been a cathedral, a mosque, a museum, and a mosque again.
A decisive siege in 1453 here ended a thousand-year empire and altered global trade.
Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk was born here and often writes about its winding neighborhoods.

title: Where mountains meet the sea and the party never ends
clues: A coastal metropolis famed for dramatic granite peaks and lush forests framing long crescent beaches.
It throws one of the world’s biggest pre-Lenten celebrations filled with samba rhythms and glittering parades.
A towering Art Deco Christ statue watches over the city from the summit of Corcovado.
It hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics and features Maracanã, once the world’s largest football stadium and site of the 1950 World Cup final.
Birthplace of bossa nova legend Antônio Carlos Jobim, whose “The Girl from Ipanema” immortalized one of its beaches.

title: Neon dreams beneath a sacred peak
clues: A mega-city where ancient temples share streets with bullet trains and tech-laden towers.
It sprawls along a wide bay, with clear winter days revealing a snow-capped giant on the horizon.
Its most famous crossroads surges with synchronized waves of pedestrians every few minutes.
Rebuilt after the 1923 Great Kanto earthquake and WWII firebombing, it has hosted the Summer Olympics twice.
Once known as Edo under the Tokugawa shogunate; birthplace of Hayao Miyazaki and home to Akihabara’s “Electric Town.”

title: Where every hour tells a story
clues: A storybook skyline of Gothic towers and red roofs rises above a winding river.
Its famed stone bridge lined with baroque statues links two historic quarters across the Vltava.
A hilltop castle complex and lantern-lit lanes have inspired writers and composers for centuries.
Crowds gather to watch an intricate astronomical clock set its figures in motion each hour.
Known for dramatic defenestrations, the 1989 Velvet Revolution, and as Franz Kafka’s birthplace.

title: Where alleys are water and history wears a mask
clues: A maze of canals and stone bridges draped over a centuries-old lagoon.
Carnival masks and gondolas glide past palazzi that blend Byzantine, Gothic, and Renaissance styles.
Nearby islands are famed for delicate glassmaking and vibrant lacework traditions.
A lion-bannered maritime republic once ruled from a pink-hued Gothic palace beside a towering campanile.
Birthplace of the Silk Road voyager whose name became shorthand for distant marvels.

title: Temples, tea, and timeless streets
clues: A city ringed by low mountains, celebrated for spring blossoms and fiery autumn leaves.
Home to hundreds of wooden temples and shrines, from hillside verandas to whispering bamboo groves.
Its summer Gion Matsuri sends towering floats rumbling through lantern-lit avenues, a tradition over a millennium old.
A landmark 1997 global climate agreement carries this city's name.
Novelist Haruki Murakami was born here, not far from vermilion gates that climb a sacred hillside.

title: A timeless stage for pageantry and pop culture
clues: A storied river threads past centuries-old markets, parks, and palaces.
A 1666 inferno reshaped its heart and inspired a towering monument.
Birthplace of a silent film legend known as the Little Tramp.
Theater lovers flock to a reconstructed Elizabethan stage celebrating the Bard.
A zebra crossing outside a famed studio became album-cover lore for a Fab Four.

title: Thermal dreams and river scenes
clues: A grand European city split by a great river and linked by stately bridges.
Renowned for steaming thermal baths housed in palatial complexes.
A skyline crowned by an illuminated neo-Gothic parliament along the waterfront.
Known for atmospheric “ruin bars” that revived crumbling courtyards into nightlife hubs.
Shook the world with a 1956 uprising and is the birthplace of escape artist Harry Houdini (Erik Weisz).

title: Where hills, fog, and free spirits meet the sea
clues: A coastal city built on steep streets where cool fog spills in from a narrow strait into a broad bay.
Its counterculture blossomed in the late 1960s, and nearby tech corridors later helped reshape modern life.
A catastrophic earthquake and fire in 1906 remade much of its urban fabric.
A former island prison here once housed Al Capone within sight of the downtown skyline.
Martial arts icon Bruce Lee was born in its historic Chinatown.

title: Where the harbor sparkles and surf never sleeps
clues: A sun-soaked waterfront metropolis famed for golden beaches and a dazzling natural inlet.
New Year’s Eve here lights up the sky as fireworks cascade over a grand steel arch.
You can stroll historic lanes in The Rocks, near the 1788 landing site of the First Fleet.
Clifftop paths link Bondi to Coogee, revealing sandstone headlands and Pacific swells.
A UNESCO-listed performing arts icon with sail-like shells crowns the harbor.

title: Where Oceans Embrace a Mountain
clues: A coastal city framed by a flat-topped massif and surf-lashed shores, famed for wineries and spring wildflowers.
Once a pivotal resupply port of the 17th-century Dutch East India Company, its past is entwined with the spice routes and the slave trade.
Penguins waddle on nearby boulder-strewn beaches, and a dramatic peninsula tumbles toward a stormy cape.
Ferries visit a former island prison that held a future Nobel Peace Prize laureate for many years.
Its skyline is defined by Table Mountain, with the colorful facades of Bo-Kaap climbing the slopes below.

title: Pearl of the Adriatic, reborn
clues: A luminous walled port city whose medieval skyline rises straight from the Adriatic Sea.
Its gleaming limestone boulevard links ancient gates, fountains, and cloistered courtyards.
Hilltop fortresses recall a 1990s siege that scarred the Old Town and is now carefully commemorated.
Within UNESCO-listed ramparts stand Renaissance palaces and one of Europe’s oldest pharmacies, dating to the 1400s.
A cable car ascends Mount Srđ above walls that famously doubled as a royal capital in a hit TV series.

title: Where bikes rule and canals sparkle
clues: A city laced with concentric waterways carved during a booming 17th‑century trade era.
Its streets hum with more bicycles than cars, threading past gabled houses and cozy cafés.
A moving World War II diary drew global attention to a hidden annex here.
Masterpieces like The Night Watch anchor a museum district devoted to Dutch Golden Age art.
Philosopher Baruch Spinoza was born here, and a famed 1637 tulip bubble still colors its lore along the Amstel.

title: Where geysers sing and auroras dance
clues: A compact harbor city set amid volcanoes, glaciers, and the midnight sun, powered by abundant geothermal heat.
Its waterfront concert hall, a shimmering glass landmark, is a beacon of contemporary Nordic design.
Just outside the city, visitors soak in milky‑blue geothermal pools and chase winter skies painted by the northern lights.
A hilltop church with a soaring, basalt‑inspired tower watches over colorful tin‑clad houses.
It hosted the 1972 Fischer–Spassky “Match of the Century” and is the hometown of avant‑pop icon Björk.

title: Where orange trees perfume the night and guitars keep time
clues: An Andalusian city where sunlit plazas and citrus-lined avenues meet centuries of Moorish and Christian influence along a great Iberian river.
Its modern makeover for a world exposition in 1992 left striking pavilions on an island in the Guadalquivir.
A royal palace here blends Mudéjar and Renaissance artistry and still welcomes visiting dignitaries.
From its docks in 1519, Magellan’s fleet set out on the first circumnavigation of the globe, completed by Elcano.
Birthplace of painter Diego Velázquez, it’s also famed for a bell tower that began as a mosque’s minaret: La Giralda.

title: Where old-world charm meets ocean breezes
clues: A sunlit port of seven hills gazing across a broad river estuary toward the Atlantic.
Yellow trams clatter up cobbled lanes to scenic hilltop viewpoints called miradouros.
A devastating 1755 earthquake reshaped the center into elegant, grid-planned Pombaline streets.
Riverside monuments in Belém commemorate the Age of Discovery and departures of explorers like Vasco da Gama.
The city nurtured the soulful tradition of fado, immortalized by iconic singer Amália Rodrigues.

title: Where empire echoes meet gelato‑fueled evenings
clues: A storied Mediterranean city where layers of antiquity, medieval alleys, and renaissance grandeur intertwine.
Its colossal stone arena once thundered with gladiatorial contests and roaring crowds.
Visitors toss coins into a famed baroque fountain here to ensure they’ll come back.
Within its boundaries sits the world’s smallest independent state and spiritual hub for millions.
Legend says twin brothers raised by a she‑wolf founded this place long ago.
